claims.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA loss expected at Rs 500-600 crores including marketing investment and no UPI incentive
Annualized people cost savings of Rs 400-500 crores expected going forward
Net payment margin outlook 5-6 bps including UPI incentive annually, 3-3.5 bps quarterly ex-UPI incentive
Take rate on financial services expected to settle at 3-3.5%
Merchant loan disbursals recovered to Rs 971 crores in April, near January levels; personal loans shifted to distribution-only model
Q4 FY24 contribution profit Rs 1,288 crores at 57% margin; EBITDA before ESOP Rs 103 crores; UPI incentive Rs 288 crores
Marketing spend in Q4 was half of normal; restarted in Q1; device deployment rates recovering toward previous levels
Targeting at least one profitable quarter in current fiscal year at EBITDA break-even before ESOP cost and excluding UPI incentives
Expect EBITDA break-even before ESOP cost and before adding UPI incentive
Expect payment processing margin of 3-3.5 bps excluding UPI incentive and 5 bps+ including UPI incentive
Target high double digits or close to 20% EBITDA margin over next 3-4 years
Capex this year will be meaningfully lower than last year due to device refurbishment and redeployment
Merchant loan disbursement seeing pent-up demand surge but remaining disciplined due to lender prudence
Personal loan disbursement focused on large tickets; secured lending pilots underway for LAP, gold loans, loan against securities
Net take rate on DLG merchant loans expected to be north of 5% over loan life, similar to non-DLG loans
Aiming to become sustainably free cash flow positive before deciding on cash return framework
Contribution margins back near 55% without UPI incentives, expected to be new norm
Expect very meaningful profitability relatively soon with tailwinds from merchant payments, lending and cost improvements
Personal loan disbursements of Rs 1,600-1,700 crores last quarter; new lending partners added but not yet ramped up
Merchant lending demand huge; focus on unlocking more capital through DLG arrangements
Active sales employees stabilizing at 30,000-31,000; productivity per employee enhancing through AI, headcount to grow slowly
Merchant transactions reached 1,000 crore in December 2024 out of 1,232 crore total transactions
RuPay credit card on QR gives disproportionately more revenue on acquiring side versus consumer side
Plan to aggressively expand merchant acquiring as it drives consumer acquisition through a flywheel effect
DLG model accounts for approximately 80% of merchant loan disbursements in the quarter
No target mix for DLG vs non-DLG; indifferent between models and open to partner preference
International expansion will focus first on merchant side payments and SME credit in Middle East and Southeast Asia
Up to ₹20 crores investment per market for international subsidiaries, largely B2B with low upfront spend
International expansion will take time due to entity formation, license applications, and operations setup
DLG also used for personal loans with select lenders in collection model only, not distribution-only model
5-6 lakh merchants have loans outstanding, representing 4-5% of device base
Target to increase merchant loan penetration to 10-15% of device base over 2-3 years from current 4-5%
Three drivers of merchant loan growth: penetration increase, ticket size growth (₹1.1L to ₹2L in 3 years), and repeat loans with higher partner confidence
Payment processing margins comfortably above guided 3 bps; rental income assumption in analyst model slightly higher than actual
Personal loan disbursements FY26 expected better than FY25 unless macro worsens; driven by additional partners and rebound from lows
Capex not expected to return to FY24 levels; refurbishment savings to continue for 2-3 quarters; depreciation to reduce as FY24 high capex rolls off
Depreciation reduction expected to accelerate in FY26 as FY24 soundbox capex (2-year depreciation) rolls off
Capex expected to return to FY24 levels
Depreciation to reduce as high FY24 capex rolls off two-year soundbox depreciation schedule
Contribution margin without UPI incentives at 50-55%, with UPI incentives at 55-60%
DLG costs impacted contribution margin this quarter due to full quarter ramp-up with largest partner
Contribution margin expected to uptick as DLG costs plateau relative to overall disbursals
Very close to EBITDA before ESOP profitability; would be profitable if this quarter's UPI incentive received
Gap between EBITDA before ESOP and PAT to become basically zero in 2-3 quarters as depreciation and ESOP costs decline and interest income rises
Expect PAT profitability once EBITDA before ESOP turns profitable, possibly in next 1-2 quarters sequentially
Goal is double-digit EBITDA margin relatively soon, translating into substantial PAT
No target number for DLG quantum; board approved limits disclosed, expect board to be constructive on additional approvals given performance
In month of disbursal, sourcing fee (3-4%) slightly higher than DLG cost (<5%), not negative business; trail revenue adds significant profitability
Targets 30-35% top-line growth and 15-20% EBITDA margin for next year and longer term
Expects PAT profitability from next quarter onwards if trends continue
ESOP charge expected to be Rs 75-100 crore for next few quarters, down from Rs 169 crore last quarter
Merchant loan take rate 3-3.5% higher with FLDG; blended financial services take rate ~2% higher due to FLDG on 50-60% of loans
Total lending partners ~14; 8-10 each for personal and merchant loans with overlap
AI enabling modularization of codebase for international product-tech partnerships with minimal incremental investment
Contribution margin reached 60% in Q1 FY26, up from 50% a year ago; management guides for high-50s steady state.
Management targets 15-20% EBITDA margin over the next two to three years.
Payment services business operated at breakeven in Q1 FY26; management expects it to become a large profit driver when UPI MDR returns.
DLG-based disbursements have declined very significantly; partner AUM under DLG is down over 40%.
Both personal and merchant loan disbursals and revenue grew sequentially; mix remains roughly the same as last quarter.
Capex and refurbishment efficiency have improved significantly, supporting lower subscription revenue per device focus on lifetime value.
EBITDA margin expected to improve significantly from current ~4% by end of financial year
Merchant lending with partners is a star performer with enormous tailwinds and conservative risk management
Net device deployments lower due to pickups of inactive devices; gross deployments higher but conservative accounting writes off devices >12 months with no transactions
Soundbox charged over 2 years, EDC over 3 years; becoming more conservative on device useful life accounting
Revenue growth of 28-31% expected to continue at least at current levels in future quarters
POS provider model doing significantly less than 10,000 but more than 5,000 units per month
AI agents for small businesses will generate subscription and inference fee revenue
No material capital investment plan for AI; investments beyond $20-50M will be proactively announced
Focus shifting from bottom-line generation to revenue generation; acceleration expected on revenue-generating line items
Subscription revenues expected to be overtaken by MDR revenues in near future
Postpaid early days with tens of thousands users; targeting couple of million; 10-12M previous customers on platform
GMV growth should be higher than UPI growth (20%) driven by market share gains and improving unit economics
Expect to offset 30-40% of PIDF impact this quarter and more over time
Contribution margin may decline to mid-50s due to PIDF impact
Payment processing margin expected to stay above 4 basis points for next few quarters
EBITDA impact expected in Q4 from remaining 60% of PIDF impact not offset this quarter
Not in device deployment or rental device as business model; focus on payment and financial services
Outlook intact: positive on device growth, merchant loans, payments processing margin; expect growth acceleration and EBITDA margin improvement
Not guiding to higher payment margin numbers right now; want to see market discipline continue
Net payment margin as percentage has not gone up; GMV up 24%, revenue up 22% year-on-year
Ambition to solve market share concentration risk via organic technology plans; less than one year since regulator permission
Payment margin guidance may be revisited in next two quarters; currently on solid positive trajectory
Depreciation not expected to rise next year due to low capex last year; may increase year after as capex ramps for deployment
Targeting 250 million monetizable customers in India over next 3-4 years; current monetization machinery can handle that scale
Expects revenue growth acceleration in FY27 across payments, financial services, and marketing services recovery
Targets 15-20% EBITDA margin in 2.5 to 3 years from now
Net payment margin above 4 bps driven by product improvements enabling pricing discipline and credit instruments on UPI growing faster than GMV
Payment processing margin growing faster than device subscription revenue; lending penetration increasing offsets lower per-device subscription
Device payback periods improving significantly due to efficient acquisition, lower capex per device, and better merchant retention
Payments platform expansion to dramatic larger TAM is obligation; cost optimization focused on product and platform creation with reducing costs
Expect significant operating leverage and EBITDA margin expansion over the next year due to revenue growth acceleration and lower indirect expenses
Achieved 30-40% offset of PIDF impact in Q4; confident of near full offset over time through sales and subscription revenue optimization
No material capital investment plan for AI data centers; will rent compute and run own models instead
Merchant lending growth driven by base expansion, penetration increase, and ticket size growth each ~15%; TAM expansion may lift blended ticket size
Wealth and personal loans expected to be much bigger contributors next year; multiple visible growth drivers in financial services
Next year EBITDA expected to be significantly higher than capex; last year had 500 crores EBITDA with capex
Management has higher confidence of reaching 15-20% EBITDA margin in next 2-3 years, potentially sooner, due to revenue growth outpacing indirect expense growth and AI-driven operating leverage.
Structural EBITDA margins for the business are significantly higher than the near-term 15-20% target, but no specific long-term number is given due to growth-investment trade-offs.
EBITDA margin improved from 1% to 8% YoY in Q1 FY27, a 7 percentage point improvement, while marketing and sales/service costs grew 27% YoY.

Payment processing margin has been inching up gradually and consistently every quarter; net payment margin declined from 8.8 bps to 8.4 bps YoY due to low-engagement merchant plans and tightened revenue recognition.
Postpaid loan book ramping up roughly twice as fast as previous cycle (which took 4.5-5 years to reach ~Rs 9,000 cr); no hurdles seen to reaching prior peak over time.
Lending partner count is now double-digit for both Merchant and Personal Loans; new partners ramping well; partner capital availability is 4-6x current disbursement run-rate.
Aggressively investing in consumer acquisition, merchant acquisition, and financial services expansion; AI used to dramatically optimize costs (e.g., in-house agent governing field sales).
Payment processing margin inching up gradually and consistently every quarter
Tightened revenue recognition policy on certain businesses had slight impact
Overall growth meaningfully better than 22% in FY27
Indirect expenses to grow much slower than revenue despite sales and marketing investments
Long-term terminal value massive; AI makes organization leaner; incremental revenue from marketing and financial services at very high EBITDA margin
Merchant payments plus merchant loans payback periods improving; business getting significantly more profitable despite PIDF going away
Device deployment pace of 25-30 lakhs additions per year to continue; additional investments could push it higher
Consumer revenue growth not far behind merchant side; tailwinds in personal loans, Postpaid, wealth, and P2P driving better LTV
Broad-based accelerated growth across payments and financial services for both merchant and consumer business
Net payment margin improved from 8.5 to 9 due to exit of a large negative contribution margin customer
EBITDA expected to continue expanding next quarter despite DLG drag; absolute EBITDA to grow quarter-on-quarter
Higher capex in first half will increase depreciation in FY28; investments driven by strong payback on engagement, retention, financial services revenue
Indirect expenses target to grow at less than half of contribution margin growth over 3-4 quarters; free cash flow to track EBITDA with capex guidance next quarter
claims.value: less than half of revenue growth

claims.statement: Depreciation YoY not up much; higher capex in H1 for engagement, retention, financial services monetization; payback visible on service costs and capex
